recognize_zh: 薄層血片中可見三種瘧原蟲時期：白箭頭是正常大小紅血球內的小環狀體，黑箭頭是被寄生而變大、形狀不規則並帶棕色色素的變形體滋養體，藍箭頭是充滿細小棕黑色瘧色素的大型圓形配子體；受感染紅血球變大是間日瘧（P. vivax）的特徵。
features: Ring stage (white arrow): delicate cytoplasmic ring with a single chromatin dot in a normal-sized red cell
Trophozoite (black arrow): irregular amoeboid parasite with brown pigment in an enlarged, distorted red cell
Gametocyte (blue arrow): round parasite filling an enlarged red cell with scattered fine brown-black hemozoin pigment
Infected red cells enlarged compared with uninfected cells; Schüffner stippling faint at this resolution
Low parasitemia with single infections per cell; no banana-shaped gametocytes
describe_en: Thin peripheral blood smear shows intraerythrocytic parasites at several developmental stages. A ring form with a single chromatin dot is present within a normal-sized red cell, an amoeboid trophozoite with brown pigment occupies an enlarged irregular red cell, and a round pigmented gametocyte fills an enlarged red cell. Parasitemia appears low, and there are no multiply infected cells or crescentic gametocytes. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium vivax infection.

ddx.vs: P. falciparum shows numerous small rings in normal-sized cells, multiple infections, appliqué forms and banana-shaped gametocytes, with mature trophozoites rarely seen.
P. ovale also enlarges red cells but produces oval cells with fimbriated edges and more compact, less amoeboid trophozoites.
P. malariae infects normal or small red cells and forms band-shaped trophozoites and rosette schizonts without enlargement or stippling.
Babesia forms small pleomorphic rings and tetrads (Maltese cross) without hemozoin pigment or gametocytes.
